content.title: CMR findings and diagnostic significance (excerpt)
main_findings: At baseline: T1-weighted (inflammation, injury) and T2-weighted (oedema) sequences, extracellular volume and LGE within 2 weeks after symptom onset. [refs 956, 960]
At follow up: LGE to evaluate the degree of scarring, T1 and T2 to identify persistent inflammation.
diagnostic_significance: At least one T2-based criterion (global or regional increase of myocardial T2 relaxation time or an increased signal intensity in T2-weighted images), with at least one T1-based criterion (increased myocardial T1, extracellular volume, or LGE) in the acute phase.
Only one (i.e., T2-based or T1-based) marker may still support a diagnosis of acute myocardial inflammation in an appropriate clinical scenario, albeit with less specificity in the acute phase.
A negative T1/T2 scan does not exclude a still ongoing inflammatory process in the chronic phase.
content.footnote_a: It takes at least 3 months before CMR signs of oedema (secondary to inflammation in the acute phase/baseline) disappear. At 6 months, T1 or T2 signs of oedema should have disappeared if inflammation would be completely absent. Still, the absence of T1 or T2 oedema does not exclude chronic low-grade inflammation.
content.figure_20_caption: Figure 20: Management of patients with heart failure and acute myocarditis.
content.figure_20_description: Flowchart: initial assessment with clinical history, signs and symptoms, ECG, laboratory, echocardiography, CMR imaging, coronary CT/CAG. Branches include treatment of CAD if present, HF treatment, clinical stabilization, consideration of EMB if doubt about diagnosis, consideration of immunosuppressive therapy or anti-infection treatment if suspected auto-immunity/infectious/toxic causes, and consideration of MCS if indicated.
content.notes: Page focuses on CMR imaging criteria for myocarditis (T1/T2/LGE) and management flowchart; no gene names are present on the page.
